analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 602-606) and docs/reference/model-registry-format.md (line 120-122, plus a date bump). The edits describe the macOS weight-hash reader. Each file is now read uncached, with a reader thread one 4 MiB chunk ahead of SHA-256 (OverlappedFileDigest, two page-aligned buffers per file). PageCache.drop still follows each read. The documented behavior says the same bytes are hashed, the aggregate SHA is unchanged, existing fallbacks are retained and any failed file prevents a successful aggregate. I identified no security-relevant change to the weight-hash verification contract (T-012, T-027, A-004), so there is no new attack surface.

The remaining units in the patch are unchanged context from the same file: the prefix cache (T-041), model cache location, environment controls and the hold socket. I saw no changes to them in the supplied hunks and no regression.

Unverified contract: the source files OverlappedFileDigest.swift and WeightHasher.swift were not supplied. Whether the implementation matches the docs is therefore unverified. Specifically, the code behind the claims that full-file coverage and error propagation are kept, and that two buffers per file are used under 4 concurrent workers, was not examined. A source pass on those Swift files should confirm that overlapped reads cannot truncate or skip bytes, drop errors, or leave a race between the reader thread and the hasher. Any such flaw would weaken the weight-hash integrity check against operator weight substitution, T-012. That check is also self-reported and bounded by the existing T-012 limits.
